verses.text: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, pay close attention to what's in front of you.
If your appetite tends to take over, hold it back as if there were a knife at your throat.
Don't crave the ruler's fancy food. That meal can fool you.
Don't wear yourself out trying to get rich. Be wise enough to know when to stop.
Why fix your eyes on something that won't last? Wealth sprouts wings like an eagle and flies off into the sky.
Don't eat with a stingy person or crave their fancy food.
They're counting the cost the whole time. “Eat and drink!” they tell you, but they don't mean it.
You'll throw up what you ate, and all your kind words will have been wasted.
Don't bother speaking wisdom into a fool's ears. They'll just look down on what you say.
Don't move an old boundary stone or take over fields that belong to children without a father.
Their Defender is strong. He'll take up their case against you.
Take instruction to heart and listen closely to words that give you knowledge.
Don't hold back correction from a child. The proverb says the rod of discipline won't kill them.
That discipline, it says, can save their life from Sheol.
My son, if your heart grows wise, my own heart will be glad.
I'll rejoice deep down when your lips say what's right.
Don't envy people who sin. Spend your whole day revering the LORD.
There really is a future for you, and your hope won't be cut off.
Listen, my son, and grow wise. Keep your heart on the right path.
Don't hang around with people who drink too much wine or stuff themselves with meat.
Drunkards and gluttons end up poor. Being half asleep all the time leaves them dressed in rags.
Listen to your father who gave you life. Don't look down on your mother when she grows old.
Buy the truth and never sell it. Get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
A father takes great joy in a child who does what's right. A wise child makes their father glad.
Let your father and mother be glad. Let the woman who gave birth to you celebrate.
My son, give me your heart and keep your eyes on the way I live.
A prostitute is like a deep pit, and an unfaithful wife is like a narrow well.
She waits in hiding like a robber and draws more people into unfaithfulness.
Who's in trouble? Who's grieving? Who's fighting and complaining? Who has bruises for no reason and bloodshot eyes?
People who spend hours drinking wine, people who go looking for mixed wine.
Don't get caught staring at the red wine as it sparkles in the cup and goes down smooth.
In the end it bites like a snake and poisons like a viper.
Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will come up with confusing thoughts.
You'll feel like someone lying in the middle of the sea or stretched out high on a ship's rigging.
“They hit me and it didn't hurt! They beat me and I didn't feel it! When will I wake up? I'll go looking for another drink.”
